$comment: Scheduled posting (flag post-schedule, D310 proposed). Each auto-queued YouTube upload goes up private with status.publishAt = the next free slot: max(latest future scheduled publish time on the channel, latest slot Ujwalam already gave out) + intervalHours, but never earlier than now + minLeadHours + marginMinutes (with nothing scheduled the first clip gets exactly that). Before an upload session starts or resumes, the slot must still be at least minLeadHours ahead; before every chunk, at least marginMinutes ahead. Every chunk request is aborted chunkDeadlineSeconds before the slot (no byte is sent after that), and the final chunk only starts when its estimated transfer time fits (slowest chunk measured in this upload, else fallbackKbps; chunkDeadlineSeconds must be less than marginMinutes x 60). Otherwise the upload stops and the clip gets a new slot (an unfinished upload session is dropped; Google discards it). The channel read covers at most maxPages x pageSize newest uploads; if the channel has more, nothing is scheduled (fail closed) until maxPages is raised. D314 (user 2026-11-09): a queued clip whose time is less than minLeadHours away and has no upload session gets now + minLeadHours + marginMinutes again (exactly 1 h cannot pass the session check), and every later queued clip without a session is re-chained intervalHours apart from it, never earlier than the latest fixed time (channel post, uploaded clip, open session, failed slot) + intervalHours. A slot more than maxAheadDays ahead is not given out: the clip waits. Read by services/posting/schedule.mjs; never hardcoded. YouTube Data API quota: 1 unit per channels.list, playlistItems.list and videos.list call (1 + 2 per page).
source: intervalHours: user request 2026-11-09 ('post 6 hours ahead of the last scheduled post'). maxAheadDays: user 2026-11-09 (D314, 'can schedule upto 2 years ahead'). minLeadHours, marginMinutes, chunkDeadlineSeconds (coordinator review 2026-11-09: about 2 min), fallbackKbps, maxPages, pageSize: agent default 2026-11-09, not a user instruction; tune here.
